extracted.intended_audience: biomedical researchers, journal editors, and scholars/policy‑makers interested in peer‑review processes
extracted.subtask_description: Systematic review and network meta‑analysis of randomized trials testing interventions (author-, reviewer-, editor‑level) intended to improve the biomedical peer‑review process, evaluating effects on review quality, duration, acceptance rates, manuscript quality, and error detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the peer‑review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Main outcome assessed in 13 studies; differences between traditional and intervention‑modified peer‑review processes were pooled as standardized mean difference (SMD) in quality based on the definitions used in the individual studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality was measured using various instruments (5‑point scales, a pre‑designed form scoring 1–100, an 8‑item review quality instrument); review quality is acknowledged as subjective and not necessarily related to manuscript quality. Network meta‑analysis compared interventions by pooling SMDs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of the peer‑review process (time‑to‑decision / turnaround time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration/time‑to‑decision was a main outcome in 11 studies and compared across interventions (sometimes defined as turnaround time or time to final decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured as days to return review or days to final decision; included in network meta‑analysis (pooled as SMD). Reviewer‑level interventions were associated with increased duration (SMD, 0.15 [0.01–0.29]) except for reviewer blinding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance / rejection rate (proportion recommending rejection/acceptance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported as primary or secondary outcomes in several trials (e.g., proportion recommending rejection, outright rejection, acceptance requiring revisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate whether interventions change editorial decisions; reported both as raw proportions and comparative measures (odds ratios, relative risks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of the manuscript (post‑review) was assessed in 4 studies using either a 5‑point scale or the Modified Manuscript Quality Assessment Instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to judge whether peer‑review interventions improved the final manuscript; small positive effects reported for use of reporting guidelines/checklists and addition of a statistical reviewer in some trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of errors detected
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of deliberately placed or actual errors detected by reviewers (assessed in 3 studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an objective measure of review thoroughness; trials inserted known weaknesses/errors and compared detection rates across interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding to author identity (single‑blind vs double‑blind)
rubrics_metrics.description: Intervention where reviewers are blinded to authors' identities (author masking) to reduce bias; tested in multiple randomized trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effects evaluated on review quality, acceptance/rejection rates, and error detection. Results mixed: some studies found no effect, some found blinded reviewers less likely to reject, some found blinding improved review quality, while others found unblinded reviewers gave higher scores/acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revealing reviewer's identity / open peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Intervention in which reviewers' identities are revealed to authors or made public (including asking reviewers to sign reports or telling reviewers their signed reviews might be posted on the web).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed for effects on review quality, rejection recommendations, and time taken to write reviews. Findings were mixed (no consistent quality benefit; sometimes increased time to write reviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of a statistical reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigning an additional statistical reviewer to manuscripts to improve methodological assessment and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two trials tested this; Cobo et al reported improvement in manuscript quality (mean rating change), while Arnau et al found no effect in primary analysis but effect in per‑protocol analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reporting guidelines / checklists (e.g., CONSORT, STROBE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Intervention where reviewers/editors are prompted to use reporting guidelines or checklists during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cobo et al found the use of reporting guidelines during peer review improved manuscript quality modestly (MD, 0.33 'as reviewed'). Generally considered a small but positive effect on manuscript reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer training and mentoring (workshops, self‑taught modules, pairing with seniors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interventions including face‑to‑face workshops, self‑taught modules, and mentoring of new reviewers by senior reviewers to improve review quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trials found small or transient improvements (self‑taught and face‑to‑face showed short‑term gains; mentoring showed modest effect size). Many training effects were not sustained long term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing reviewers with authors' conflict‑of‑interest disclosures (unblinding authors' disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Intervention providing reviewers with authors' COI statements to assess whether knowledge of disclosures affects review quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: John et al (BMJ) found no meaningful effect on manuscript quality from revealing disclosures (MD, 0.04; 95% CI, −0.05 to 0.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial pre‑screening / early screening (editor‑level intervention)
rubrics_metrics.description: In‑house editorial screening before external review to triage manuscripts and reduce unnecessary peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Johnston et al found early screening significantly decreased review time (48 days to 18 days) and reduced number of required external reviews; considered a positive effect on efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asking reviewers to accept before manuscript assignment / shorter invitation acceptance period
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational changes asking reviewers to commit before being sent the manuscript or reducing the time allowed to accept an invitation (e.g., 1 day vs 3 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitkin & Burmeister and Provenzale found reduced turnaround time in some implementations; however, 'ask‑first' can increase decline rates and not always reduce total processing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting reviewers before review (prior reviewer contact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Intervention of calling or contacting reviewers before assignment to improve turnaround time or engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mixed results: Neuhauser & Koran found contacting reviewers increased turnaround time; Pitkin & Burmeister found reduced time to file reviews but no net effect on overall processing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback from editors to reviewers (written feedback)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors provide written feedback to reviewers about their performance to improve subsequent review quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Callaham et al tested this and found no significant change in review quality after providing feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic exchange of reviews (exchange comments among reviewers from different regions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Intervention where reviewers' comments are exchanged between groups (e.g., Indian and non‑Indian reviewers) to test cross‑learning effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Das Sinha et al reported no significant effect on review quality from informing reviewers that comments would be exchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of reviewers' ability to detect intentionally placed errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Using manuscripts with known/inserted errors to objectively measure reviewers' detection performance as an outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several trials used this method (Godlee et al, Okike et al, Schroter et al) as an objective proxy for review thoroughness; results varied by intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessors of review quality (who rates reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review quality was assessed by different raters across trials (editors, authors, statisticians, or blinded assessors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of assessor is a methodological variable: studies extracted 'assessors of review quality' and timing/method of assessment; heterogeneity in assessors contributes to subjective variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review quality assessment instruments / scoring modalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruments used in trials included 5‑point Likert scales, a pre‑designed form scoring up to 100, an 8‑item review quality instrument, and reviewer score ranges (e.g., 0–10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differences across instruments were standardized via SMD for meta‑analysis. The specific instrument and scale affect interpretation and comparability of outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of interventions by process level (author‑level, reviewer‑level, editor‑level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interventions were categorized by the level at which they operate (author, reviewer, editor) for analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Network meta‑analysis grouped interventions by level; reviewer‑level interventions ranked best for improving review quality (rank score 0.88) compared with author‑ and editor‑level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias assessment (Cochrane Collaboration's Tool)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of included randomized trials was assessed using the Cochrane Collaboration's Tool for assessing Risk of Bias in randomized trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study quality assessment informs confidence in pooled results and was summarized in supplemental Table S2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical and evidence‑synthesis methods and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Network meta‑analysis used random‑effects models (generic inverse variance), Cochran's Q for inconsistency, rank scores for probabilities, comparison‑adjusted funnel plots and Egger test for publication bias, leave‑one‑out and fixed‑effect sensitivity analyses. Statistical significance set at two‑tailed 0.05 without multiplicity adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These analytic choices determine interpretation of pooled SMDs and robustness checks; authors reported heterogeneity/inconsistency analyses and sensitivity checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criteria for trials in review
rubrics_metrics.description: Randomized trials comparing different peer‑review interventions at author‑, reviewer‑, and/or editor‑level, aimed at improving quality of the peer‑review process by exploring at least one of the following outcomes: acceptance/rejection rate, quality of the manuscript, quality of the review, duration of the peer‑review process, number of errors detected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case reports, conference presentations, editorials, expert opinions, and studies not comparing review processes were excluded. Full‑text screening and dual data extraction were performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive caution: subjectivity and heterogeneity in 'quality' definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors note that 'quality' of peer‑review is subjective by definition and heterogeneity in interventions, journals, fields, outcome definitions, and instruments remained across trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results should be interpreted recognizing limited generalizability, potential underpowering for individual interventions, and that review quality may not equate to manuscript quality or clinical importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective outcome reporting recommendations (report both short‑term and long‑term effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trials reported short‑term vs sustained effects (e.g., training effects were often transient and not maintained on later papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating interventions, report durability of effect (immediate vs long term) and downstream impacts (e.g., time costs, acceptance rates).
